ZBoard is a self-hosted basic panel for Zero proxy services. It manages nodes, users, subscriptions, orders and traffic usage, with optional plugins for additional capabilities.

This release candidate establishes capability-owned application boundaries, unifies durable background jobs, fixes shared-pool subscription validation and improves account security and plugin interaction.

## Highlights

- Move HTTP and background orchestration behind explicit identity, commerce, entitlement, metering, messaging, network, experience and platform capabilities. Ownership inventory and architecture guards now reject new unowned routes, writes, plugin operations and cross-domain transaction boundaries.
- Run administrator tasks, node publication, Zero event consumption, credential expiry, database migration and plugin tasks through one durable runtime with persisted attempts, lease fencing, bounded retries, cancellation requests, timeout recovery and diagnostic history.
- Add planned schedule slots, missed-run and timezone policies, unique triggering and weighted dispatch lanes so high-frequency work cannot indefinitely suppress lower-frequency maintenance.
- Expose scoped integration credentials and capability discovery/invocation without placing payment-channel logic in the core. Payment providers remain optional plugins and are not bundled in this RC.

- Import Clash and sing-box subscriptions with HTTPS latency-test URLs using Zero's default HTTP probe. Preserve HTTP probe URLs and node TLS settings. Failed synchronization continues to retain the previous pool.
- Restore the built-in change-password form. Confirm identity-management operations once per login for five minutes; password changes invalidate that confirmation and plugins never receive the password.
- Keep plugin forms open through transient connectivity failures. Use consistent retry states and frameless slot containers, allowing content to shrink to its actual height.

- Read plugin names, descriptions and maintainers from the admitted plugin directory; discover versions, packages and release notes from each publisher repository. No repository-root marketplace.json is required. Stable, RC and Dev channels remain separately selectable.
- Maintain shared proxy pools from Zero, Clash/Mihomo, sing-box or node-link subscriptions (including Base64). Choose a client preset or custom User-Agent, synchronize manually or on a schedule, and publish only after parsing and Zero validation succeed. Failed synchronization preserves the last working pool.
- Open publisher version selection directly from an installed plugin.
- Preserve manual RAW editing and fix empty-group serialization for single-node pools.
- Install or switch to an exact marketplace version, or import `.zbplugin` packages for private and development use. Package identity, signatures, digests, platform compatibility and admitted capability boundaries are checked before installation.
- Manage plugin configuration, activation, upgrades, rollback and removal in the console. Version changes apply data migrations atomically, and failed migrations preserve the previously working version and data.
- Connect third-party identity providers through plugins and let users link or unlink an external identity. Disabling or uninstalling a plugin retains its configuration, private data and core-owned identity links; destructive data removal remains a separate explicit action.
- Use clearer account navigation on smaller screens and consistent announcement card layouts.
- Set a forwarding entry's subscription name directly and arrange forwarding entries alongside direct services.
- Open subscription access information from the administrator's order view.

## Deployment

The HTTPS probe conversion is a compatibility fallback for current Zero kernels, not HTTPS probing support. Its default target is `http://www.gstatic.com/generate_204`; raw Zero configuration is not rewritten. OAuth content sizing and publisher-label improvements require updating the separately installed OAuth plugin as well.

Use the exact RC image tag shown in this release. Back up the database, deployment configuration, encryption keys, plugins and managed rules before updating. Preserve the previous image for rollback.

The ordered migrations add proxy-pool subscription settings, durable job attempts and schedule-planning metadata. Back up first, run one RC instance with `-migrate-only`, then start application instances after migration completes; do not let multiple blue/green instances race non-transactional MySQL DDL. Recreate the application container after changing its image or environment because a container restart does not load changed Compose environment values. Preserve the existing credential encryption key.

Subscription import supports a subset of client configurations; unsupported transports or options fail explicitly. The new converters do not support custom WebSocket Host, obfuscation plugins or every client-specific extension. Routing and DNS rules are not imported into shared pools.

This is a release candidate for deployment validation. Online payment channels belong in plugins; this release exposes core order and integration capability boundaries but does not include a payment plugin.
